subject: Re: Connectivity options for NovaMed private deployment - peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN
messages:
From: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@novamed.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Roger Li <roger.li@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private deployment connectivity — quick request

Ben — thanks for taking this. We're in scoping for a Private (VPC) deployment of Redwood's inference nodes and need your recommendation for how to connect our on-prem network to Redwood's VPC. High level requirements: HIPAA compliance, predictable latency (< 40 ms typical), limited public IP footprint (we can only open a handful of static IPs), and no sustained egress of PHI over public internet paths. We also have overlapping RFC1918 ranges in some of our data centers (10.0.0.0/8 in prod).

Questions:
- From an operational and compliance perspective, which is the best first choice among (1) VPC peering (cross-account), (2) PrivateLink / interface endpoints, (3) site-to-site VPN (managed S2S) — and why?
- Can PrivateLink preserve source IPs so we can do allow-listing on our side? If not, what are common workarounds?
- Any tradeoffs on latency or troubleshooting complexity we should plan for?

We're trying to avoid a long architecture back-and-forth before procurement. If you can send a short recommendation and a suggested pilot plan (what to test, expected metrics), that would be super helpful. I'm attaching our network requirements spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Claire D'Souza
Head of IT Architecture | NovaMed Health
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: novamed-network-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@novamed.com>
Cc: Roger Li <roger.li@novamed.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — quick request

Claire — thanks for the clear brief and the sheet, useful. High-level recommendation up-front: a hybrid, split-path approach tends to hit your constraints best for high-assurance private deployments. In short:

- Primary: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for inference API traffic (token/streaming calls). Rationale: PrivateLink keeps traffic on the cloud provider network, reduces public exposure, and supports cross-account access patterns without full routing exposure between VPCs. It also lets us present service endpoints behind our managed VPCs — which helps with HIPAA requirements for minimizing public internet traversal.

- Secondary: A short-lived site-to-site VPN (or managed S2S) for control-plane/admin traffic (provisioning, health checks, debugging) and for cases where you need source-IP preservation or interactive access.

- Avoid plain VPC peering for the primary path unless you want full L3 mesh and can ensure no CIDR overlap. Peering is simple and low-latency but becomes operationally risky with overlapping RFC1918 ranges (you called that out). Peering also exposes broad network-level reachability between accounts which complicates segmentation and compliance boundaries.

Key details and tradeoffs:
- Source IP visibility: PrivateLink terminates connections at the provider's endpoint and the service typically sees the endpoint ENI's IP as the source, not the original client IP. That means you lose original source IPs by default. Workarounds: (1) we add an X-Forwarded-For header at the edge if the protocol supports it (works for HTTP/gRPC); (2) run a small proxy in your VPC that preserves client IPs in the headers and forwards to the PrivateLink endpoint; (3) use S2S VPN for flows where true source IP mapping is required for allow-lists.

- Latency: PrivateLink over a regional interface endpoint generally adds a few ms relative to native VPC traffic but is highly stable. Peering is lowest-latency (no middlebox), VPN is worst and variable (depends on tunnel type and provider). For your target <40 ms, both PrivateLink and peering are typically fine if the Redwood serving VPC is in the same cloud region as your transit/edge. VPN can still hit 30–60+ ms in some setups — we can validate with a short test.

- CIDR overlap: peering fails if ranges overlap — you'd need re-addressing or NAT. PrivateLink avoids that because it uses endpoints and does not require route propagation between your VPC and ours.

- Troubleshooting and observability: with PrivateLink, debugging tends to be higher-level (connection endpoint health, DNS resolution, headers) rather than raw packet tracing. VPN/peering permit packet-level debugging but require coordination on routing tables, BGP, and firewall policies.

Suggested pilot (2–3 week):
1) Configure a PrivateLink endpoint for the inference API in your VPC (we'll provide endpoint service name). Validate tokenized request/response and streaming behavior. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, stream reconnect rate, tokens/sec.
2) Bring up a temporary S2S VPN from your edge to an admin subnet in our dedicated pilot VPC. Use that tunnel to exercise any source-IP-sensitive operations and to test mutual auth and log transfer.
3) Run traffic for 48 hours under representative load (1–5 rps to start) and collect latency/availability/cost numbers.

I've attached a short PDF with the connector pros/cons and an initial checklist. Next steps: can you confirm (a) the precise AWS/Azure region you'll colocate in, (b) whether you can host an interface endpoint (we'll provide a service name for cross-account), and (c) whether any of your data centers can do a small address carve to avoid the 10/8 overlap?

I'll loop in Jordan and Marissa to book a short technical session and to propose a mutual action plan.

— Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0127

Attachments: redwood-privatedeploy-connector-options-v1.pdf (18 pages)

From: Claire D'Souza <claire.dsouza@novamed.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Roger Li <roger.li@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — quick request

Ben — this is super helpful, thanks. A couple of clarifying Qs before we schedule the call:

1) You said PrivateLink "terminates" connections and might present the ENI IP as source. For HTTP traffic we can use X-Forwarded-For, but some of our monitoring and firewall rules rely on authenticating the source IP at the perimeter (not application-level headers). If we use PrivateLink + a tiny proxy in our VPC, does Redwood still see the original client TLS identity? Any impact on mTLS?

2) For the pilot, can you give a rough expected p95 for a small request (1k token generation) over PrivateLink vs peering vs VPN — just ballpark numbers to help our network SLAs.

3) We do have one region where we can carve a /20 out of our internal space for the pilot — that should help the peering option if we ever go that route.

Roger and I are available for a 45-min technical session next Tue or Wed morning PST.

Thanks,
Claire

Goal: show Claire two concrete options with measurements and a M.A.P. (mutual action plan) by EOD Monday so we can get the pilot started mid-next week.
